text:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing at the Prince and Princess of Wales’s country mansion, police have said.
Norfolk police are investigating the suspected break-in at Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country retreat given to William and Kate as a gift by Queen Elizabeth II after their wedding.
“Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary following an incident at a property on the Sandringham estate last night. Police were called just before 6pm following a report of suspicious activity at the address,” the force said.
“Officers attended and specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area. Two men were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass. They remain in police custody.”
It is understood no members of the royal family were at home when the alleged burglary took place.
According to the tracking site Flightradar24, a police plane left Nottingham East Midlands airport at 6.25pm on Monday, and circled an area close to Sandringham before landing back at the airport almost three hours later.
The secluded red brick Georgian mansion is on the private Sandringham estate in Norfolk and is a short drive from Sandringham House, one of King Charles’s private residences.
It has its own private swimming pool, a full-size, artificial grass tennis court and vast grounds. Kensington Palace said it would not comment on security matters.
